'''Mycheal Gerome Henry''' (born December 23, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[NLEX Road Warriors]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA). He played [[college basketball]] for [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] and [[DePaul University]].

==College career==
Henry began his college career at [[University of Illinois]] where he was recruited by [[Bruce Weber (basketball)|Bruce Weber]].<ref name="CT Transfer">{{cite web | url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-myke-henry-depaul-spt-1212-20141211-story.html | title=After transfer from Illinois, Myke Henry warmly embraced at DePaul | publisher=Chicago Tribune | date=December 11, 2014 | accessdate=November 3, 2017 | author=Ryan, Shannon}}</ref> After his freshman year Weber was fired, and new head coach [[John Groce]] used Henry sparingly as a sophomore which contributed to his decision to transfer to DePaul.<ref name="CT Transfer"/>

At DePaul, Henry scored a career high 29 points against [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] on November 30, 2014.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/11/30/depaul-stuns-sluggish-stanford-87-72/19710421/ | title=DePaul stuns sluggish Stanford 87–72 | publisher=USA Today | date=November 30, 2014 | accessdate=November 3, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===2016–17 season===
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Henry signed with [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the NBA G League for the [[2016–17 NBA Development League season|2016–17 season]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://basketball.dailyherald.com/article/20161110/sports/161119880/ | title=Plenty of familiar names play in NBA D-League | publisher=Daily Herald | date=November 10, 2016 | accessdate=November 3, 2017 | author=Mcgraw, Mike}}</ref> On May 3, 2017, After appearing in 39 games with the Oklahoma City Blue, Henry signed with [[Rayos de Hermosillo]] of the [[CIBACOPA]] league in Northwestern Mexico.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.court-side.com/news/myke-henry-deals-hermosillo/ | title=Myke Henry deals with Hermosillo | work=Court Side Newspaper | date=May 3, 2017 | accessdate=November 3, 2017}}</ref>

===2017–18 season===
On October 23, 2017, Henry returned to the Oklahoma City Blue for the [[2017–18 NBA G League season]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-announces-training-camp-roster-2/ | title=Oklahoma City Blue Announces Training Camp Roster | date=October 23, 2017 | accessdate=November 3, 2017 | publisher=NBA Media Ventures | archive-date=October 24, 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024080735/http://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-announces-training-camp-roster-2/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 13, 2018, Henry signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/sign-myke-henry-to-way-contract-180113 | title=Grizzlies sign Myke Henry to two-way contract | work=NBA.com | date=January 13, 2018 | accessdate=January 23, 2018}}</ref> On July 20, 2018, the Grizzlies waived Henry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-waive-myke-henry-180720|title=Grizzlies waive Myke Henry|work=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2018|accessdate=July 20, 2018}}</ref>

===2018–19 season===
On July 23, 2018, Henry signed a one-year deal with [[Ironi Nahariya]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Myke Henry signs with Ironi Nahariya|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/283156/myke-henry-signs-with-ironi-nahariya.html|work=Sportando.com|accessdate=July 23, 2018|date=July 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724002321/https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/283156/myke-henry-signs-with-ironi-nahariya.html|archive-date=July 24, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 7, 2018, Henry recorded 31 points in his first game with Nahariya, he shot 11-of-17 from the field, along with three rebounds in a 98–95 win over [[Hapoel Holon]]. He was subsequently named [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#MVP of the Round|Israeli League Round 1 MVP]].<ref>{{cite web|title=מצטיין המחזור הראשון: מייק הנרי|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=19420|access-date=October 9, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=October 9, 2018|language=he}}</ref> On March 23, 2019, Henry recorded a double-double of 18 points and 11 rebounds, along with three blocks and three assists in a 88–77 win over [[Hapoel Holon]]. He was subsequently named [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#MVP of the Round|Israeli League Round 23 MVP]].<ref>{{cite web|title=מצטיין המחזור ה-23: מייק הנרי|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=21006|access-date=March 26, 2019|work=basket.co.il|date=March 26, 2019|language=he}}</ref> In 33 games played for Nahariya, he averaged 14.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 steals per game.

===2019–20 season===
On September 30, 2019, Henry signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2019/09/30/thunder-add-four-players-prior-training-camp/|title=Thunder add four players prior to training camp|access-date=October 5, 2019|work=OKCThunderWire|date=September 30, 2019}}</ref> He later joined their G League affiliate, the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Gee |first1=Erik |title=Oklahoma City Blue Release Training Camp Roster. |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/oklahoma-city-blue-release-training-camp-roster/ |accessdate=December 5, 2019 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=October 29, 2019}}</ref> On December 28, 2019, Henry accumulated 24 points, nine rebounds, two steals, two blocks and one assist in a 112–89 victory over the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Myke Henry: Leads team in scoring |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/326190-myke-henry-leads-team-in-scoring/ |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 29, 2019}}</ref> He missed a game with a foot injury in January 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Myke Henry: Returns from injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/myke-henry-returns-from-injury/ |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 24, 2020}}</ref> Henry averaged 13.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Myke Henry: Scores 12 in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/myke-henry-scores-12-in-loss/ |accessdate=June 14, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 12, 2020}}</ref>

===2020–21 season===
On July 11, 2020, Henry signed with [[Pallacanestro Trieste]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{cite news |title=Myke Henry inks with Trieste |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/myke-henry-inks-with-trieste/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=July 11, 2020 |date=July 11, 2020}}</ref>

===2021–22 season===
On July 16, 2021, Henry signed with [[Champagne Châlons-Reims Basket|Champagne Châlons-Reims]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Myke HENRY signe au Champagne Basket pour une saison ! |url=https://champagne-basket.fr/actualite/myke-henry-signe-au-champagne-basket-pour-une-saison |website=Basket.fr|date=16 July 2021 |language=French }}</ref> He averaged 12.6 points per game, but was waived on January 8, 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Champagne Basket signs Orlando Coleman, waives Myke Henry |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/champagne-basket-signs-orlando-coleman-waives-myke-henry/ |website=Sportando |access-date=January 8, 2022 |date=January 8, 2022|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref>

On January 28, 2022, Henry signed with [[G.S. Iraklis B.C.|Iraklis Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mammides |first1=Chris |title=Myke Henry (ex Chalons-Reims) signs at Iraklis |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/728118/Myke-Henry-(ex-Chalons-Reims)-signs-at-Iraklis |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 24, 2022 |date=January 24, 2022}}</ref> In 12 games, he averaged 15.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.4 steals in 27 minutes per contest.

===2022–23 season===
On July 2, 2022, he signed with [[Scafati Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/myke-henry-joins-scafati/|title=Myke Henry joins Scafati|date=July 2, 2022|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 2, 2022|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref>

On December 1, 2022, he signed with [[Astoria Bydgoszcz]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]] (PLK).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Italy/news/781006/Astoria-adds-Myke-Henry-to-their-roster,-ex-Scafati|title=Astoria adds Myke Henry to their roster, ex Scafati|last=|first=|date=December 1, 2022|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=December 1, 2022}}</ref>

===2024 season===
On July 17, 2024, he signed with [[NLEX Road Warriors]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) as the team's import for the [[2024 PBA Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tiebreakertimes.com.ph/tbt/nlex-signs-ex-memphis-grizzlies-player-myke-henry-for-pba-govs-cup/307492 |title=NLEX signs ex-Memphis Grizzlies player Myke Henry for PBA Govs' Cup |website=Tiebreakertimes.com.ph |date=July 17, 2024 |accessdate=July 18, 2024 }}</ref>

==International career==
Henry joined a Chicago-based [[3x3 basketball]] team composed of [[Stefhon Hannah]], Kavon Lytch, and [[Alfonzo McKinnie]] who went undefeated in the 2016 USA Basketball 3x3 National Championship that was played Aug. 27–28 at the United States Olympic Training Center in Colorado Springs, Colorado. The team represented the United States at the [[2016 FIBA 3x3 World Championships – Men's tournament|2016 FIBA 3x3 World Championship]] in [[Guangzhou]], [[China]] and won the silver medal.<ref name="USA">{{cite web | url=https://www.usab.com/history/3x3-men-and-womens/3x3-mwc-2016.aspx | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107012919/https://www.usab.com/history/3x3-men-and-womens/3x3-mwc-2016.aspx | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 7, 2017 | title=Third FIBA 3x3 World Championship for Men – 2016 | publisher=USA Basketball | date=2017 | accessdate=November 3, 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
When Henry was 17 years old, his 15-year-old brother DJ was shot and killed as an innocent bystander to gang violence.<ref name="CT Transfer"/>
